items.caseName: Jai Prakash Singh v. State of Uttar Pradesh & Ors.
items.headline: Senior can't be paid less than junior in same post
items.text: Two lecturers were appointed the same day in 1990 at a college in Aligarh, but the junior drew higher pay after getting advance increments. The Court held the gap had no valid basis and violated the guarantee of equality.
items.why: Pay parity between colleagues holding the same post applies even when increments come through a court order.

items.caseName: Shivendu Pandey v. State of U.P. & 11 Ors.
items.headline: UP told to frame compensation policy after Lucknow fire
items.text: UP has no compensation policy for deaths in incidents other than natural calamities, such as the June 2026 Lucknow fire that killed 15 young people. The State must frame one with clear criteria and pay an injured survivor's medical costs.

items.caseName: Balveer Singh v. State of U.P. & Ors.
items.headline: Senior citizens tribunal can't void gift deed for forgery
items.text: A tribunal under the Senior Citizens Act cannot declare a gift deed void on a claim of forgery. That dispute belongs in a civil court.

items.caseName: Nitin Mishra v. Union of India & 6 Ors.
items.coram: Arindam Sinha & Satya Veer Singh, JJ.
items.headline: Lone NEET-UG answer key objection rejected
items.text: Disputed questions go to an expert only when facts justify it. A single objection, already rejected by the NTA and backed by no other candidate, did not.

items.caseName: Mohammad Jalaluddin v. State of U.P. & 3 Ors.
items.headline: Owner can't plead ignorance to save beef-laden vehicle
items.text: Once the meat is confirmed as beef, the statutory presumption applies to an owner travelling in the vehicle. He failed to rebut it, so the confiscation stands.

items.caseName: M/s. Pharmed Limited v. Union of India
items.coram: Manish Pitale & Shreeram V. Shirsat, JJ.
items.headline: NPPA's blanket drug price ceiling quashed
items.text: A 2009 NPPA notification applied ceiling prices to any formulation containing a scheduled drug. The court quashed it: the DPCO required a formula-based ceiling price notified for each formulation, which was never done.
items.why: Drug price controls must follow the DPCO's product-by-product method.

items.caseName: Aman @ Aman Ibrahim Khan v. The Commissioner of Police, Pune
items.coram: Sarang V. Kotwal & Ranjitsinha Raja Bhonsale, JJ.
items.headline: Detention can't rest on a guess that bail is likely
items.text: A detention order under the Maharashtra MPDA Act was set aside. Saying the detenu would probably get bail, without material to back it, is not a valid ground.

items.coram: Parth Prateem Sahu & Sushma Sawant, JJ.
items.headline: Unchallenged WhatsApp chats prove cruelty; divorce granted
items.text: Family Courts are not bound by strict rules of evidence. Unchallenged WhatsApp messages showing mental cruelty could be relied on, and the wife was granted divorce.

items.caseName: Praveen Kumar Yadav v. Smt. Priyanka Yadav
items.coram: Parth Prateem Sahu & Sachin Singh Rajput, JJ.
items.headline: Husband's visits don't prove wife left without cause
items.text: Repeated visits to the wife's parental home or a legal notice do not show her refusal to return was unreasonable. Her allegations of ill-treatment and dowry demands justified living apart.

items.headline: Rape conviction overturned after 13 years
items.text: The survivor said her clothes were soaked in blood, but forensic tests found none. The court called this a positive contradiction, not a mere lack of corroboration, and set aside the kidnapping and rape conviction.

items.caseName: Union of India & Ors. v. Himanshi & 34 Ors.
items.coram: C. Hari Shankar & Vinod Kumar, JJ.
items.headline: Unfair means must be proved candidate by candidate
items.text: The SSC cancelled candidatures in the 2019 CHSL exam and imposed seven-year debarments. The court found the evidence against the candidate did not hold and ruled a one-size-fits-all approach unlawful.

items.caseName: Equitas Small Finance Bank Ltd. v. Mrs Nirmala Bai Shanthilal & Ors.
items.headline: Bank can't disown its counsel's settlement statement
items.text: The bank's cheque-bounce case was closed after its counsel reported a settlement before the Magistrate and the Lok Adalat. A year later it called that statement unauthorised; the court refused, warning that would cause chaos.

items.caseName: Smt. Simran Kaur v. State (Govt. of NCT of Delhi)
items.headline: Travel refused, but pregnant accused's care protected
items.text: An Afghan national under investigation was not allowed to go to the UK to give birth. Police must ensure the probe does not delay her medical care during her twin pregnancy.

items.caseName: Yeshwant Shenoy v. Bar Council of Kerala
items.headline: Notice on challenge to Bar Council committees
items.text: An elected member says the Chairman announced the statutory committees of the XIII Bar Council of Kerala without holding elections. Notice was issued to the Council and its Chairman; the case returns on 1 October.

items.caseName: Sanjay Kumar Yadav v. State of Bihar & Ors.
items.headline: An FIR alone can't sink an arms licence
items.text: The Collector refused a builder's licence only because a criminal case was pending, in which he was later acquitted. The refusal was quashed: a threat to public safety must be shown.

items.caseName: Navin Kumar v. State of Bihar & Ors.
items.headline: Department's own lapses can't block contractor's dues
items.text: Poor supervision and record-keeping by the department is no ground to withhold payment for completed work. About ₹19.8 lakh in dues and security deposits must be paid with 5% interest.

items.caseName: Heera Mani v. State of Rajasthan & Anr.
items.coram: Sanjay K. Agrawal, CJ & Vinit Kumar Mathur, J.
items.headline: Absence due to long illness is not wilful misconduct
items.text: A constable's absence during prolonged tuberculosis was not deliberate, so his termination was quashed. His widow gets all service and retiral benefits.

items.caseName: Rapti v. State of Uttarakhand & Anr.
items.headline: Stepfather must maintain the child he knowingly accepted
items.text: A man who married knowing of his wife's son from an earlier marriage took on responsibility for the boy. Maintenance was raised, with ₹10,000 a month for the son until he comes of age.
